phases.label: AI Literacy Nonprofit
phases.description: Build the legal foundation, earn tax-exempt status, launch pilot workshops, and secure first-round grant funding. This phase is about proving the concept and establishing credibility.

phases.label: Innovation Incubator
phases.description: Launch the incubator program supporting rural entrepreneurs building AI-powered businesses. Run cohorts, host demo days, and expand partnerships with universities and economic development organizations.

phases.label: Investment Fund
phases.description: Establish a community investment fund to provide capital to rural AI startups. Leverage relationships built in Phases 1 and 2 to attract institutional investors and government backing.

milestones.title: Initiative Conceived
milestones.description: The idea takes shape — AI literacy for rural South Carolina. Vision crystallized for a three-phase initiative: nonprofit, incubator, and investment fund.

milestones.title: SC Trip & Networking
milestones.description: Travel to South Carolina. Meet Kim Bowman at SCRIN, visit UofSC Office of Innovation and Tech Incubator, connect with Rep. Bradley's office, and begin building the local partner network.

milestones.title: File Articles of Incorporation
milestones.description: Submit Form NP to the South Carolina Secretary of State. The official legal birth of the organization. Cost: $32.50. Expected processing: 1-2 business days.

milestones.title: Get EIN from IRS
milestones.description: Apply for Employer Identification Number (EIN) on IRS.gov. Free and instant. The EIN is the nonprofit's tax ID — needed for bank accounts, grant applications, and everything else.

milestones.title: Organizational Board Meeting
milestones.description: Hold the first official board meeting. Approve bylaws, elect directors, adopt conflict-of-interest policy, and authorize opening a bank account. This is the moment the organization truly comes alive.

milestones.title: 501(c)(3) Application Filed
milestones.description: Submit IRS Form 1023-EZ (for organizations expecting under $50K/year) or Form 1023 (full version) for federal tax-exempt status. Cost: $275 (1023-EZ) or $600 (1023). Processing: 3-6 months.

milestones.title: Google for Nonprofits Application
milestones.description: Apply for Google for Nonprofits program. Unlocks free Google Workspace (email, Drive, Docs), $10,000/month in Google Ad Grants, YouTube Nonprofit Program access, and Google Maps Platform credits.

milestones.title: First Grant Application Submitted
milestones.description: Submit the first major grant application — targeted at the OpenAI People-First AI Fund. This marks the transition from formation to active fundraising.

milestones.title: First AI Literacy Workshop Pilot
milestones.description: Host the first AI literacy workshop in a rural South Carolina community. This pilot validates the program model, generates impact data for grant applications, and begins building the community reputation.

milestones.title: 501(c)(3) Determination Received
milestones.description: Receive the IRS determination letter granting tax-exempt status under Section 501(c)(3). This unlocks: donor tax deductions, Google for Nonprofits, most major grants, and nonprofit bank rates. A major milestone.

milestones.title: First Major Grant Awarded
milestones.description: Receive the first major grant award (target: OpenAI People-First Fund or USDA Rural Business Development Grant). This validates the fundraising strategy and provides runway for Phase 2 planning.

milestones.title: First Incubator Cohort Launch
milestones.description: Launch the inaugural cohort of the rural AI innovation incubator. Target 8-12 entrepreneurs from rural South Carolina communities. Provide mentorship, AI tools training, business development support, and connections to the broader innovation ecosystem.

milestones.title: First Demo Day
milestones.description: Host the first incubator Demo Day — a public showcase where cohort companies present to investors, press, partners, and community members. Modeled after Y Combinator Demo Day but rooted in rural South Carolina.

milestones.title: Fund Structure Established
milestones.description: Legal structure for the investment fund established. This may be a community development financial institution (CDFI), a donor-advised fund, or a separate LLC/LP structure. Legal counsel and financial advisors engaged.

milestones.title: First Investment Made
milestones.description: Deploy the first capital investment into a rural South Carolina AI startup — ideally an alumnus of the incubator program. This completes the flywheel: literacy → incubation → investment → impact.

activities.title: Nonprofit Formation
activities.description: All the legal paperwork to officially create the nonprofit: name reservation, Articles of Incorporation, EIN, initial report to SC DOR, bylaws drafting, and organizational board meeting.

activities.title: Tax-Exempt Application
activities.description: File IRS Form 1023-EZ or 1023 for 501(c)(3) status, then file SC state tax exemptions and charitable solicitation registration upon receiving determination letter. The process takes 3-6 months.

activities.title: Infrastructure Setup
activities.description: Set up the operational infrastructure: nonprofit bank account, website, email domain, social media accounts, Google for Nonprofits application, project management tools, and financial tracking system.

activities.title: Grant Applications Round 1
activities.description: Submit Tier 1 grant applications: OpenAI People-First AI Fund, Google.org/aiEDU Rural Catalyst, and Microsoft/OpenAI Societal Resilience Fund. Each requires a tailored narrative, budget, and supporting documents.

activities.title: Workshop Pilot Program
activities.description: Design and deliver the first series of AI literacy workshops in rural South Carolina communities. Start with 2-3 pilot workshops, gather participant feedback, refine curriculum, and document impact metrics for grant applications.

activities.title: Partnership Building
activities.description: Develop formal partnerships with SCRIN, SC Nexus, UofSC, HBCUs, 4-H chapters, local libraries, school districts, and Rep. Bradley's office. Partnerships unlock grants, provide credibility, and build the community network.

activities.title: Incubator Design
activities.description: Design the innovation incubator program structure: cohort size, curriculum, mentor network, application process, graduation criteria, and funding model. Research best practices from successful rural incubators.

activities.title: First Incubator Cohort
activities.description: Run the inaugural incubator cohort from launch through Demo Day. Weekly programming, mentor sessions, pitch practice, and culminating public showcase. Target: 8-12 rural SC entrepreneurs.

activities.title: Grant Applications Round 2
activities.description: Submit Tier 2 grant applications with the enhanced credibility of completed workshops and the incubator launch: NSF BPC, EDA Tech Hub via SC Nexus, USDA RBDG, and SC Commission for Minority Affairs.

activities.title: Fund Research & Planning
activities.description: Research legal structures for the investment fund, engage financial and legal advisors, study successful rural investment fund models (e.g., Runway, Opportunity Alabama), and develop the fund thesis and investor pitch.

activities.title: Fund Launch
activities.description: Establish the legal structure, raise initial capital commitments, develop deal flow pipeline from incubator alumni, and make the first investment into a rural SC AI startup.
